handback.t:
H10 (R5-B) done. Board entry with rerun commands: C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\h10_board_entry.md (proposed patch: results/h10_proposed_patch.md, no src change needed). No src edits, no commits, no downloads. Cargo target C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r3, MiniLM on disk only.

WHAT IS REAL vs SYNTHETIC
- Real: all text (docs of ~700 vendored crates = world A with 6831 paragraph docs; ruvnet docs + our docs + doc comments = world B with 4181 docs), the queries (section titles H, held-out real sentences S), the keyword vocabulary, and the topic clusters (k-means on real MiniLM embeddings).
- Synthetic: the typos injected into queries (QWERTY single-edit model) and EVERY routing outcome (agent competence per real cluster, keyword prior, Bernoulli draws).
- Only n=10 genuine human misspellings (mined from the docs) exist as queries; descriptive only.
- "Validated on real traffic" is still NOT met.

1. SPELL-CORRECTION + RETRIEVAL on real text (protocol: tune seeds 1-8, held-out A 31-60, confirm A 61-90, confirm B 61-90 on independent text with frozen picks; paired t-CI over seeds; Holm over 100 tests per split; also a bootstrap over distinct queries)
- g1's spell gain replicates: +0.015 MRR / +0.010 hit@1 at 25% typo queries (g1: +.016..+.020), Holm win in all 3 splits. It is concentrated in short heading queries (+.024..+.028 MRR) vs long sentences (+.004..+.006). Query-cluster bootstrap CIs exclude 0.
- Spell is not free: Holm-significant loss on clean queries (-.0016..-.0020 MRR in A; n.s. in B), because real words missing from the doc vocabulary get altered (1-3% of clean headings, 9-14% of clean sentences).
- g1's "dense >> BM25" does NOT replicate: in A, MiniLM ties BM25 (MRR +.010 and +.004, n.s.; bootstrap CI of dense+spell minus BM25+spell about [-.014,+.021]), and BM25 wins on sentence-to-paragraph queries. Dense wins in B (+.022 MRR) but g1 had +.06/+.07.
- The bigger lever on real text is dense+BM25 z-score hybrid (alpha .7, tuned on A tune seeds), not spell: +.040 / +.048 / +.028 MRR over dense+spell (Holm wins; bootstrap +.033..+.059 in A, +.014..+.041 in B). g1 had +.012.
- Spell on top of hybrid adds +.015..+.017 MRR, all on typo queries.
- g1's "transductive query-log" speller rule is irrelevant (S2 = S1 to 4 decimals).
- Real-typo n=10: dense MRR .108 -> .176 with spell (equals the hand-fixed text). Direction only.
- Absolute hit@1 is low (~.2, 6.8k near-sibling fragments), so read relative effects only.

2. COMPACTROUTER vs f64 recommended router on a real-text-shaped replay (task = real sentence, features = its rare content words, topic = real embedding cluster; 8 worlds: 4 real, 2 long-tail vocabulary, 2 shuffled controls; K12/6 agents and K48/32 agents)
- TOST at the pre-declared ±0.005 AND ±0.003: CERTIFIED in all 8 worlds, in every split (smoke, held, confirm, pooled 31-90, 160-seed power split).
- Max |mean diff| 0.0003; compact-f64 bit-identical (0e0); hash32 variant same verdicts.
- Caveat: routers beat the keyword-prior-only baseline by only +.002..+.013 here, so the test has little learning signal to damage; weaker evidence than g3's worlds.
- Decisions/s on the real long-tail vocabulary (paired ratio, noisy shared box): compact is 2.6x to 4.6x faster per decision than f64 (about 260k-420k vs 64k-156k decisions/s).

3. SERVE with real-text payloads
- Replies, exit codes and final state files are BYTE-IDENTICAL to HEAD 52f936c in all 14 scenarios (14 base-vs-base controls identical, harness self-test detects a 1-byte change).
- Payloads: real keyword features, whole real paragraphs as feature strings, mutation fuzz applied to real requests, 1 MiB boundary lines.
- The CLI-interleaved scenario is g6's and still uses synthetic features.
- Decisions/s with real payloads (paired ratio, background CPU 60-87%, bad replies 0): lockstep N=1 478 -> 3330 (6.9x), N=4 1323 -> 3993 (3.0x), pipelined N=1 640 -> 6442 (10.2x), stdio 1.10x (no measurable gain, as in g6).

SURVIVED real text: spell gain and its clean-query cost; hybrid beating dense-only; CompactRouter equivalence; serve byte-identity and the 3-10x TCP speedup.
WEAKENED or FAILED: dense >> BM25 (tie in A); "spell is the whole system gain" (hybrid is larger); g1's transductive speller rule (irrelevant).

Caveats:
- Relevance is structural (section membership / source paragraph), not human-rated.
- t-CIs over seeds resample one finite query pool and are too narrow for dense-vs-BM25; use the bootstrap CIs.
- World B reads live repo files; use the saved fixtures (md5 in results/h10_corpus.md5) rather than rebuilding.
- Baseline build overwrites release/neural-mesh.exe in the shared target dir.
